themes.A: Physical/zonal topology and I/O responsibility boundaries
themes.B: Central/HPC compute, consolidation, virtualization and mixed criticality
themes.C: In-vehicle networking, Ethernet/TSN/CAN XL and deterministic communication
themes.D: Runtime, middleware, service/data contracts and platform interoperability
themes.E: Cloud-to-edge development, CI/CD, integration, diagnostics and validation lifecycle
themes.F: Functional safety, cybersecurity, isolation and trust boundaries

candidate_assignments.rationale: Use as the cross-cutting decision framework for how far centralization should proceed and where local/distributed constraints remain.
Use as a synthesis anchor for deterministic/reliable SDV building blocks and the coupling between compute, communication and dependability.
Core evidence for mixed-criticality integration on centralized HPC and for the safety/isolation constraints on consolidation.
Core empirical evidence for virtualization and microservice trade-offs on SDV compute platforms.
Published automotive-specific TSN profile is a primary standard anchor for deterministic Ethernet.
Core non-Ethernet backbone/sub-backbone counterpoint that prevents the network chapter from collapsing into an Ethernet-only story.
Core evidence for stable vehicle-data semantics as software/service boundaries move independently of physical ECU topology.
Core implementation-platform evidence for the open software foundation emerging around high-performance SDV ECUs.
Core evidence for variant-aware CI/CD and the development-lifecycle implications of SDV architecture.
Supports the mixed-criticality section with an ASIL-decomposition/resource-allocation optimization example.
Supports hardware-enforced isolation and trust-boundary discussion for consolidated automotive compute.
Supports the physical/zonal edge of the Ethernet story with multidrop 10BASE-T1S automotive specifications.
Supports the network chapter with channel/component constraints that keep logical architecture tied to physical automotive Ethernet reality.
Provides research evidence for dynamic QoS negotiation under strict latency constraints on vehicular TSN.
Primary project evidence for the SOME/IP implementation layer used in service-oriented in-vehicle communication.
Use the release series as maturity chronology rather than a separate architecture story.
Provides comparative middleware performance evidence for the consequences of choosing different communication substrates.
Supports cloud-native/service-mesh influence on in-vehicle service architecture without making it the survey thesis.
Supports interoperability discussion at the AUTOSAR Adaptive/ROS 2 boundary.
Industry-perspective evidence is useful for AUTOSAR Adaptive friction and adoption context, but remains partial and should not anchor normative claims.
Supports cloud-native-to-deterministic-runtime discussion with a concrete SOAFEE/DENSO implementation claim.
Use the launch announcement to establish the start of the open core-stack initiative, not as a separate technical package.
Use the S-CORE release series to show maturation across communication, safety, integration and module-maturity mechanisms.
Supports software-driven integration and configuration as a bridge between platform architecture and development tooling.
Supports automated platform configuration/integration and its resource/safety constraints.
Supports the validation-lifecycle section with a central-car-server Vehicle-in-the-Loop/digital-twin example; preserve its partial evidence caveat.
Supports diagnostics as a modular software-defined vehicle service and lifecycle concern.
Supports service authentication/authorization and trust-boundary discussion using Internet-standard security mechanisms.
Evidence is credible but the power-packet/sensorless-drive architecture is peripheral to the survey's E/E responsibility-boundary thesis and would dilute the 48-page volume.

abstraction_probe.finding: The shared role safety model is reusable. Domain-specific thematic grouping should remain a separate overlay because the production Selection contract does not preserve Screening topic lanes into Architecture Input.
future_profile_candidates: theme assignments carried as an Architecture overlay
